subject: Acme long-context eval follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bradley <t.bradley@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Thanks — follow-up and next steps on long-context evals

Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

- Need: evaluate model behavior on long medical records (avg ~15k tokens, some docs up to 80k) and ensure summarization fidelity + stable truncation behavior.
- Success metrics we discussed: recall of key entities (meds, dosages) >= 95% on core set; abstractive summary preserves adverse events and care plan; truncation should not silently drop last 20% of context without clear signal.
- Constraints: data must remain in Acme's VPC for initial evals (private deployment).

Recommended next steps from our side:
1) Share prompt set + sample docs — please send a small batch (5–10) redacted records.
2) We'll run a 2-model baseline (open Llama-2-70b-quant and an instruction-tuned long-context variant we host) and return a comparison report with token counts, truncation points, and summary diffs.
3) Schedule a 30m follow-up week of Feb 15–19 to go over results and tradeoffs (latency vs. context window).

I attached the prompt set we typically start with and a short benchmark PDF that explains our long-context evaluation methodology. Dev — feel free to add anything I missed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood_long_context_benchmarks.pdf
From: Tom Bradley <t.bradley@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 02:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up and next steps on long-context evals

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying points from our side:

- We can do a redacted batch of 8 records next week. Most records are episodic (multiple visits in one file) so the important info can be spread across the document.
- Our main concern: we saw models in-house that appear to "drop" final sections when summarizing long docs — the summary looks fine but later we discovered the discharge instructions were omitted. We want a concrete way to detect/troubleshoot that (e.g., token-level truncation logs, or a heuristic that flags summaries where last 20% contains unique entities).
- For compliance, initial evals must run in our account/VPC. Are there minimum infra requirements for the private deployment?

We can target a demo call on Feb 16 (PST). Please confirm what you need from us to get started.

—Tom
Tom Bradley
Director of AI Platforms, Acme Corp
t.bradley@acme.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up and next steps on long-context evals

Tom — quick technical answers: 

1) Private deployment requirements: for the initial eval (70b quant + long-ctx variant) we'd recommend a single 4xA100(80GB) GPU pool or equivalent (depends on batching); we can provide an ARM/AMI and IaC templates to spin up in your VPC. We'll also send a security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence as part of onboarding.

2) Truncation visibility: our runtime logs token consumption per-request and records the last KV cache index used. For evals we produce a per-response trace that shows: input token distribution, first/last token index kept, and whether the runtime applied chunking/streaming fallback. We'll include a small analyzer that compares entity coverage in the last N tokens vs. the summary output and will flag discrepancies above your threshold.

3) Models: for a starting point we suggest:
   - redwood-long-65b-instruct (our long-context variant, 64k native context)
   - llama-2-70b-quant (open baseline; good throughput)

Attached: a short benchmark PDF and the prompt set Marissa mentioned. I'll prepare an IaC snippet for the VPC deployment and send by EOD.

—Dev
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Tom — great, Feb 16 at 10:00am PST works for us. Calendar invite incoming.

To make sure the eval returns actionable signals, a couple of requests from our side:
- Please include 1) the 8 redacted records (S3 link or upload to our secure intake in your VPC), 2) one negative example where you saw the summarize-then-drop behavior, and 3) any internal evaluation scripts you currently run (if helpful).
- We'll run: accuracy/recall checks for key entities, truncation trace report, token-cost estimates, and a qualitative summary fidelity check against a small human-labeled set.

Next steps:
1) Tom sends sample data + any internal scripts by Feb 14 EOD.
2) Dev sends IaC and SOC2 evidence links by Feb 12 EOD (Dev, ping if you need input).
3) Marissa/Aditya will send calendar invite and prep deck.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marissa
